response: Yes, continuous physical training can counteract the aging effect on myoelectric fatigue. Regular exercise has been shown to improve muscle function, reduce fatigue, and delay the onset of age-related muscle decline. As people age, their muscles undergo natural changes that can lead to decreased strength, endurance, and increased fatigue. However, studies have found that long-term physical training can help mitigate these effects by improving muscle fiber composition, increasing capillarization, and enhancing neuromuscular transmission, ultimately reducing myoelectric fatigue in older adults.
